overview: Dry and mild through Saturday across the West. A weak system brings rain and high snow Sunday into Monday, and a stronger, colder storm follows late Monday into Tuesday. Washington and Oregon see several rounds of snow and rain from Thursday into early next week.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Dry and mild through Sunday morning, with ridgetop gusts of 45 to 60 mph. A weak low brings snow above 8,000 feet Sunday night into Monday, then a colder storm arrives late Monday night into Tuesday, with snow levels falling to near 7,000 feet. Forecasters disagree on how wet that storm will be. Mammoth could see 14 inches Tuesday. The NWS is calling for more, 22 to 37 inches from Sunday night through Tuesday night.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A moderate atmospheric river, a long band of moisture off the Pacific, brings widespread rain through Friday. A weaker system follows Friday, and a brief dry spell comes Saturday. Snow levels run high in Oregon, so the Cascades see little there. Crystal Mountain has 13 inches so far. The NWS is calling for more, 10 to 24 inches from Friday through Monday night.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A Pacific system arrives Friday afternoon, bringing snow to western mountains through Saturday, with a winter storm warning in effect. Jackson Hole has 12 inches so far, and the NWS is calling for 20 to 40 more from Thursday night through Tuesday night. Winds gust near 60 mph along the Wind Corridor Friday.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Dry, mild weather holds through Saturday, with dense valley fog overnight. A wet system arrives Sunday, bringing light mountain snow above 7,500 feet and gusty south winds along the crest. Another storm follows Monday into Tuesday. Kirkwood has 10 inches so far. The NWS is calling for 20 to 31 inches from Sunday through Tuesday night.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Mostly rain, heavy at times, through Friday, with winds gusting to 50 km/h. Snow is limited to higher terrain. Sun and cloud return Saturday and Sunday before rain returns Sunday night and Monday. Whistler has 13 inches so far.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Rain changes to showers Thursday, then a mix of sun and cloud through the weekend. Rain or snow returns Sunday night into Monday. Whitewater has 7 inches so far, with Fernie and Revelstoke also reporting snow and rain showers.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Dry through Friday, with snow starting late Friday and running through Saturday across northern and central Colorado. A winter weather advisory covers the Park and Elkhead mountains, and another covers central mountains, where up to 8 inches is possible by Sunday morning. Steamboat could see 6 inches Saturday. The NWS is calling for more, 6 to 13 inches from Friday night through Tuesday night.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Freezing rain and icy travel in Vermont and northern New York tonight, with a freezing rain warning for Tremblant Friday and Saturday. Light mountain snow follows over the weekend, with rain below 2,500 feet. Another frontal system brings rain and snow Sunday night into Monday. Jay Peak has 6 inches so far, and a winter weather advisory runs through Friday.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
